# AI Migrations

> Lessons from products migrated to another language or framework with AI, for anyone running a
> large project with AI agents.

**Unofficial. No company named here endorses or is affiliated with this project.** Company and
product names describe the subject of each case only. Summaries are in our own words and link to
their primary sources.

<!-- disclosure: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 16 of the 24 cases used Claude models or Claude Code (Bloomberg, Ping.gg, GitHub, Checkly, Intel, Bun, GitLab, Mindstone, Datadog, Lutz Leonhardt, PagerDuty, Ladybird, Christopher Chedeau, Spotify, Robert Marshall, Slack; 6 others leave the models unstated), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case. GitHub, Intel, Mindstone and Ping.gg also used other vendors' models; where a source compares outcomes by model, that is its author's own unaudited report, and no lesson ranks vendors.

## What it does

<!-- contents: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Now: 24 cases (Slack, Zalando, Airbnb, Google, Robert Marshall, Spotify, Christopher Chedeau, Ladybird, Uber, PagerDuty, Lutz Leonhardt, 1Password, Datadog, Mindstone, GitLab, Bun, Asana, Intel, Checkly, Temporal, Shopify, GitHub, Ping.gg, Bloomberg), 152 lessons on 16 aspect pages, and a checklist of 12 questions.
<!-- /contents -->

- **Cases** ([cases/](cases/)): one file per migration done with AI, from engineering posts,
  papers and official repositories. Each says what AI did, what rule-based tools and people did,
  how the result was checked, the numbers with their basis, and what went wrong, including what
  the source leaves out.
- **Lessons** ([lessons/](lessons/)): what the cases teach about large AI-driven work, by aspect
  (reviews, tests, orchestration, rollout, cost). The sources stay migrations; the lessons apply
  more widely.
- **Checklist** ([checklist.md](checklist.md)): questions a coding agent can measure on a
  repository before a migration, each with a check and the evidence behind it.
- **Pitfalls** ([pitfalls.md](pitfalls.md)): what the old stack does without being asked, by kind
  of move, and seams for moving in steps.
- **For agents** ([llms.txt](llms.txt)): one line per case and lesson page, so an agent reads
  only what it needs.

[index.md](index.md) lists everything. [log.md](log.md) records what each update covered.

## Try it

Open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) in your project and pick one of two routes:

- [Planning a migration](#planning-a-migration): run the checklist on the project you are
  thinking of moving to another language, framework or major version.
- [Learning from the lessons](#learning-from-the-lessons): compare how AI agents work in any large
  project with what these migrations taught. Lessons tagged "Old system as oracle: no" are the
  place to start; each is still judged by its own words.

In both, step 1 only reads your project and changes nothing: you get numbered proposals, each
with a one-word recommendation (do, later or skip) and a reason, and you choose. Run step 1 in a
fresh session and paste step 2 in that same session. Steps 2 to 4 are optional; run each revisit
in a fresh session.

### Planning a migration

#### Step 1: review

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow it. Run the checklist on this project: measure every question with its check; do not judge from memory. Report in the checklist's report format: each answer with its evidence and the cases behind it, then a go or no-go with the main risks. Give each proposal a recommendation of exactly one word, do, later or skip, with a reason. Change nothing.
```

Before applying anything, check step 1's claims: a proposal can rest on a wrong reading of your
project.

#### Step 2: apply

To accept the agent's recommendations, paste:

```text
Apply the proposals you marked "do". Do the work the way this project normally runs work (yourself, or by briefing workers). Before changing anything, write the record https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md defines in docs/migration-review.md with each chosen proposal's baseline: how often its problem has happened so far, with the evidence. For each proposal, first state its "Check now" and its "Event that proves it"; it is applied when the check now passes (waiting for first use), proven only once later work shows the event. Where the owner left a question unanswered, assume the default the report states and record the assumption. Then complete the record, with every proposal, including the later and skipped ones, and the newest entry of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/log.md this review covered.
```

To choose yourself, replace the first sentence with "Apply proposals 1, 3 and 5."

#### Step 3: revisit later

When the collection has grown (llms.txt names a newer log entry than your record) or after a few
weeks of work, run a revisit in a fresh session. It stops at once if nothing is new or due; else
it re-checks the record against its baselines, then measures and proposes only what is new since
your record's log entry. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md and follow its revisit step. Read docs/migration-review.md. Compare the log entry it names (date and title) with the newest entry llms.txt names; if they match and no item is due for re-check, tell me and stop. Re-check each item: rerun its "Check now" unchanged, look for its "Event that proves it" in the work since, compare with its baseline, and mark it exactly "proven", "still waiting", "stopped holding" or "not shown" (its event cannot be seen yet), with the numbers. For each log.md entry newer than the record's, read its changes/ file (the lesson IDs and checklist questions it added, changed or removed); open only those, and measure them; do not judge from memory. List the applied lessons a newer lesson now contradicts or supersedes, and the items whose lesson changed. Propose only the new or changed ones, earlier "later" items, applied items that stopped holding and what that list found, each with exactly one word, do, later or skip, and a reason. Update the record in its existing layout and name in it the newest log.md entry you read, by date and title. Change nothing else until I choose.
```

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A [field report](docs/field-reports.md) says which questions foresaw the problems you hit and
which missed them; it is how the checklist improves. Wait until an item has met its problem since
its baseline (proven, or stopped holding); until then the record says nothing has happened yet.
Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/migration-review.md, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

### Learning from the lessons

#### Step 1: compare

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt and follow its route for large AI-driven work that is not a migration, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md. Compare the lessons with how this project's agents and sessions work today; measure from the repository and its history, do not judge from memory. Report in that page's report format: numbered proposals, each with the lesson ID, what the project does now, the change, its cost, and the check that would prove it. Give each proposal a recommendation of exactly one word, do, later or skip, with a reason. Change nothing.
```

#### Step 4: share what you learned (optional)

A field report from this route says which lessons held in a project that is not a migration; it
tells us which lessons and "Old system as oracle" tags to re-check against their cases. Wait until
an item has met its problem since its baseline. Nothing is posted until you say yes. Paste:

```text
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md and follow it. Draft a field report from docs/ai-lessons-review.md, naming which lessons held and which did not, scrub it, and show me the exact text before posting. If no item has met its problem since its baseline, write that in the record with the date and do not draft a field report yet.
```

## Contributing

Corrections are welcome: a wrong number, a broken link, a summary that misreads its source. Open
an issue; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) describes the case
format and the rules every file follows.
